title: Service boundaries & SLO onboarding checkpoints - Q2 2026
summary: Working checklist and collaboration notes for onboarding services to the Reliability Program. Focus: explicit service boundaries, measurable SLOs, telemetry gaps, and minimally-invasive rollout for Redwood hosted inference endpoints.
body:
Context:
This doc captures checkpoints and a lightweight schedule for onboarding a service to the Reliability Program and SLOs. It is intended for service owners, product+engineering, observability, and platform teams. The goal is to reduce ambiguity around what is in-scope, how SLOs are measured, and who needs to do what for a safe rollout.

Principles (short):
- Keep SLOs observable with existing telemetry first; add instrumentation only when necessary.
- Define service boundary by API surface and downstream dependencies, not by repo layout.
- Prefer small, targeted SLOs (one for availability, one for latency, one for correctness/regression signal).
- Rollouts should be reversible and have objective rollback criteria.

Minimum required artifacts from a service:
- Service boundary doc (one-page): endpoints, dependent services, data stores, third-party calls.
- Current traffic envelope: 7-day and 30-day query counts, peak RPS, typical payload sizes.
- Error taxonomy: which errors are user-visible vs background and which should be included in 'error budget'.
- Existing dashboards and dashboards owners.
- Owner contact and escalation matrix.

Suggested starter SLO templates (examples for Redwood inference endpoints):
- Availability SLO: Successful-response-rate for /v1/generate and /v1/chat >= 99.9% over 28 days (exclude 4xx from clients if intentional rate limiting).
- Latency SLO: P95 server processing latency <= 300ms for small generation requests (<= 512 tokens) over 14 days.
- Quality/regression proxy: Rolling prompt-set match rate >= 95% (requires integration with evaluation harness).

Measurement definitions & queries (observability team help required):
- 'Successful-response-rate' = count(status_code in 200..299 AND not backend-timeout) / count(total_requests - excluded_internal_probes)
- 'Server processing latency' = request_end_time - request_start_processing_time (NOT include queue wait). If start_processing is missing, fallback to request_end - request_start and mark as 'approximate'.
- Tagging: every request must carry service_version, model_variant, and request_tier for meaningful slicing.

Telemetry gap checklist:
- [ ] request_start_processing_time exists
- [ ] model_variant tag present
- [ ] upstream dependency latency/error metrics mapped
- [ ] synthetic probes configured (two regions minimum)
- [ ] alert thresholds for symptom indicators (error rate spike, steady latency increase)

9-week lightweight onboarding cadence (recommended):
- Week 0: Kickoff + Service boundary alignment (1h session). Deliverable: one-page boundary doc.
- Week 1: Telemetry discovery + quick gaps list. Deliverable: telemetry gap checklist filled.
- Week 2: Draft SLOs & measurement queries. Deliverable: SLO proposal doc with owner signatures.
- Week 3: Implement missing instrumentation (up to 2 sprints/PRs). Deliverable: merged PRs and test dashboards.
- Week 4: Synthetic probes + baseline data collection (14 days). Deliverable: probe dashboards.
- Week 6: Readiness review and canary config. Deliverable: canary runbook and automated rollback steps.
- Week 8: 28-day evaluation window start (for availability) or 14-day for latency; begin soft alerting.
- Week 9+: Finalize SLO, switch to operational cadence, add to Reliability Program tracker.

Cross-functional roles (RACI-style in plain text):
- Service owner: R (responsible) for boundary doc, SLO sign-off, rollback decisions.
- Dev team: R for instrumentation, PRs, dashboards.
- Observability: A (accountable) for measurement queries, probes, and alerts.
- Platform/SRE: C (consulted) for canary automation, routing policies, and cost impact.
- Product: I (informed) for customer-facing communications and prioritization.

Rollout & rollback criteria (practical):
- Canary run (48-72h) acceptable if: no sustained error-rate increase > 0.5% above baseline, latency within 10% of baseline, synthetic probes green.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate spike > 2% absolute increase sustained for 5 minutes OR P95 latency degradation > 50% for 10 minutes.
- Manual rollback: if quality regression proxy shows > 3% delta on core prompt-set.

Communication templates (short):
- Canary start (Slack): "Canary for svc-x SLO onboarding starting now. Owners: Aisha, Marcus. Watch /svc-x/dash. If error rate > 2% or latency spike >50% for >10m, rollback. See runbook: <link>."
- Incident notice (customer-facing): "We are investigating degraded performance for inference endpoints. We will update in 30 minutes."

Post-onboarding expectations:
- Post-mortem for any canary failure within 48 hours.
- SLO review at 30 days after finalization; consider tightening or splitting SLOs if stable.
- Monthly SLO health summary included in Reliability Program sync.

Open questions / decisions to be made:
- What is the standard SLO evaluation window across all hosted endpoints? 28d for availability vs 14d for latency?
- Should 4xx be excluded always or only when client-side rate limits are documented?
- How do we handle model-variant-induced latency differences in composite SLOs? Recommend per-variant slicing first.

Next steps (owner assigned):
- Aisha: schedule kickoff with svc-x and Observability (by 2026-02-25).
- Marcus: prototype measurement queries and synthetic probe (by 2026-03-04).
- Sofia: draft user-facing comms templates and onboarding checklist page (by 2026-03-01).

Quick links & references:
- Reliability Program tracker: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Telemetry guide: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/docs/telemetry-guidelines.md
- SLO definition template: CONFLUENCE-5678

Notes to self:
- Keep rollout lightweight; many teams get blocked by oversized dashboards. Start with the smallest set of metrics that prove the SLO.
- Encourage teams to pick one signal that maps to user pain for quality/regression rather than trying to capture correctness perfectly at first.

Version history:
- v0.1 2026-02-18 initial draft (Aisha)
- v0.2 2026-03-02 added canary criteria and telemetry queries (Marcus)
